We have mass spec: m/z 194.0862 (intensity 100) as base peak. Likely molecular ion. So molecular weight ~194.086. The isotopic pattern shows small M+1 (13C) at 195.0896 intensity 13% (approx 13% natural abundance of 13C). That matches a molecule with about 1 carbon? Actually 13C natural abundance 1.1% per carbon. 13% suggests about 12 carbons (12*1.1% =13.2%). So about 12 carbons. Also M+2 at 196.0835 intensity 32.8% maybe due to 2 13C? Actually probability of two 13C ~ (n choose 2)*(1.1%)^2 ~ (12*11/2)*0.000121 =66*0.000121=0.008 =0.8% not 33%. So M+2 likely due to chlorine (Cl-35/37 isotopes). Chlorine gives M+2 about 32% (since 37Cl is 24.2% natural abundance). Indeed M+2 intensity ~33% matches presence of one chlorine atom. So molecule contains one chlorine (35Cl base, 37Cl M+2). The M+1 from 13C is 13% as above. So formula likely C?H?Cl? maybe O? Let's compute exact mass: 194.0862. Let's consider possible formula: C12H?Cl? Let's compute monoisotopic mass: C12 = 12*12.0000 = 144. H? each 1.007825, Cl-35 = 34.968852. So mass = 144 + n*1.007825 + 34.968852 = 178.968852 + n*1.007825. Need 194.0862 => difference = 15.11735. Divide by 1.007825 ≈ 15.0. So n ≈15 hydrogens. So formula C12H15Cl (monoisotopic mass = 144 + 15*1.007825=144+15.117375=159.117375 +34.968852=194.086227. matches! So formula C12H15Cl.

DBE: DBE = C - H/2 + N/2 +1 =12 -15/2 +1 =12 -7.5 +1 =5.5? Wait halogen counts as hydrogen. For formula with halogen, treat Cl as H. So effective H' = H + Cl = 15+1=16. DBE = C - H'/2 + N/2 +1 =12 -8 +1 =5. So DBE=5. That suggests aromatic ring (4 DBE) + one additional double bond or ring. Likely a chlorinated cyclohexyl phenyl? The simulated spectra for ClC1(CCCCC1)c2ccccc2 gave C13 NMR deltas: 150.5, 132.3, 129.3, 128.67, 128.67, 126.46, 126.46, 34.40,34.40,25.60,22.40,22.40. Our experimental carbon NMR: 147.00, 133.90, 128.91,128.91,127.68,127.68,44.06,34.54,34.54,26.90,26.90,26.18. Compare: experimental has 12 peaks (some duplicates). Simulated has 12 peaks as well. Values similar: aromatic carbons around 147,133.9,128.9,127.7 etc. Aliphatic carbons: experimental 44.06, 34.54,34.54, 26.90,26.90,26.18. Simulated: 34.40,34.40,25.60,22.40,22.40 plus maybe 44? Actually simulated list includes 34.40,34.40,25.60,22.40,22.40 and also maybe 44? Not present. But experimental has a 44 ppm carbon likely a carbon attached to chlorine (C-Cl). Simulated structure ClC1(CCCCC1)c2ccccc2 is a chlorinated cyclohexyl phenyl (chlorine attached to cyclohexane carbon). That carbon attached to Cl would be around 44 ppm, matches experimental 44.06. Simulated didn't list 44 maybe omitted? Actually list includes 34.40 etc. Could be missing due to rounding.

Proton NMR not yet measured. But we have mass spec and carbon NMR. The candidate structure seems plausible: chlorophenyl cyclohexane (chlorine on cyclohexane). The SMILES we simulated: "ClC1(CCCCC1)c2ccccc2". Let's validate formula: compute formula for that SMILES. Use get_formula.
